title: The audit's own skip census undercounts skip sites 6x (27 declared, 166 actual) because it greps only `pytest.skip(` and misses 139 unittest-style skip sites
claimUnderTest: evidence/test-results-summary.txt says '## Static census of skip/xfail markers (skips are runtime, so this is the declared set)' and lists 27 lines, framing that as the complete declared skip surface behind a 6,278-pass green run.
observed: The census regex matches only `pytest.skip(` and `pytest.mark.skipif`. The suite is majority-unittest, and 139 further skip sites use `self.skipTest(...)` / `unittest.skipIf(...)`, which the census cannot see. Total is 166 sites in 43 files. The three largest are invisible to the census entirely: tests/api/test_launch_readiness.py (26 sites), tests/api/test_single_curve_live.py (17), tests/api/test_draft_capital.py (17). A skipped test and a passing test are byte-identical in `pytest -q` output, and no workflow asserts a minimum collected/passed count, so the declared figure is what a reader uses to size the risk.

reproduction.actual: TOTAL skip sites: 166 in 43 files; top files test_launch_readiness.py=26, test_single_curve_live.py=17, test_draft_capital.py=17, test_source_monitoring.py=15, test_picks_end_to_end.py=12

userImpact: A maintainer reading the green run sizes the false-confidence surface at 27 self-skipping assertions and moves on. The real figure is 166, concentrated in exactly the modules that assert against the live board (launch readiness, the single-curve invariants, the draft-capital workbook). tests/api/test_draft_capital.py is NOT livedata-marked, so its 17 skip sites sit in the BLOCKING tier: if openpyxl or CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx goes missing, the only check that a Sleeper-traded pick moves auction dollars in the right direction evaporates into a green PR.

priorFinding.note: Prior counted 157 in 30 files at commit 9c5d972; I measure 166 in 43 files at e96c06ef with a superset regex (adds unittest.skipIf/skipUnless). The new half is that the MASTER AUDIT'S OWN evidence file re-introduced the undercount at 27.

whatWorks: Every skip carries a human-readable reason string; none are bare. tests/consensus_edge/test_panel.py's 10 shallow-clone skips are correctly gated on an explicit `panel.is_shallow()` and do NOT fire in CI (pr-validation.yml:65 and deploy.yml:43 both set fetch-depth: 0).
rootCause: The census was produced by a grep for `pytest.skip(` against a test suite that is majority `unittest.TestCase`.
requiredRepair: Replace the census regex with the union pattern above, and add a `--collect-only` floor assertion to pr-validation.yml so a drop in executed-test count fails the gate.

title: tests/roster_intel/test_real_rosters.py — 22 tests written to catch 'a constant masquerading as a score' execute in NEITHER CI tier, because the file they need is gitignored
claimUnderTest: The module docstring: '``_positional_coverage`` once returned exactly 100.00 for all 12 teams — a constant masquerading as a score. Synthetic fixtures would not have caught that, because it only collapsed on live data. Every headline metric is therefore asserted to VARY across the real league.' Line 29 adds: 'Marked ``livedata``: they read the live snapshots and are excluded from the blocking suite.'
observed: The module is doubly excluded and runs zero times in CI. (1) `pytestmark = pytest.mark.livedata` (line 59) removes it from the blocking gate `pytest tests/ -x -m "not livedata"` — measured: 22 deselected, 0 collected. (2) The advisory tier `pytest tests/ -m livedata` DOES collect all 22, but the module fixture skips on `data/public_league/nfl_players_full.json` (line 63, gate at 86-87), which is gitignored by `.gitignore:45 data/` — only `data/ros/` is re-included — and is not tracked by git. Measured: 22 skipped. So the exact defect class this file exists for (a metric collapsing to a constant only on live data) has no automated detector at all, in either tier.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && echo '--- blocking tier ---' && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/roster_intel/test_real_rosters.py -m 'not livedata' -q --co 2>&1 | tail -2 && echo '--- advisory tier ---' && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/roster_intel/test_real_rosters.py -m livedata -q -rs --tb=no 2>&1 | tail -2 && echo '--- is the input tracked? ---' && git ls-files --error-unmatch data/public_league/nfl_players_full.json 2>&1 | tail -1
reproduction.expected: 22 tests execute in at least one tier
reproduction.actual: blocking tier: 'no tests collected (22 deselected)'; advisory tier: '22 skipped in 0.12s'; git: "did not match any file(s) known to git"

userImpact: /rosters and the terminal render positional coverage, fragility, clogger value, entry rate, lineup score, positional deficit and the competitive-window probabilities. If any of these collapses to a constant across all 12 teams — the exact failure the file records as having happened once already — every team shows the same number and a manager makes roster decisions off a metric that is no longer measuring anything. Sixteen named guards, including `test_fragility_varies_and_is_not_the_old_constant`, `test_trajectory_axis_is_live_not_pinned` and `test_eligibility_join_is_complete_on_the_real_league`, are all inert.

priorFinding.note: Prior counted skips in aggregate. It did not identify that this module is BOTH livedata-deselected and artifact-skipped, i.e. zero executions in either tier rather than 'advisory only'.

whatWorks: The two other inputs the fixture needs — data/sleeper_last_good.json and data/ros/aggregate/latest.json — ARE tracked, so the gate that fires is precisely the untracked one. The skip message names the missing artifact honestly.
rootCause: `data/` is gitignored wholesale with a narrow re-include for `data/ros/`; `data/public_league/nfl_players_full.json` (12,201 entries per the docstring) was never added to that re-include list, and nothing cross-checks livedata-marked modules against whether their inputs survive a clean checkout.
requiredRepair: Either `git add -f data/public_league/nfl_players_full.json` and re-include it in .gitignore (it is a static Sleeper player dump, same class as the already-tracked exports/latest/), or make the fixture fail rather than skip when the module is run in the advisory tier. Adding a CI assertion that the livedata tier reports zero skips would catch the whole class.
dependencies: Coupled to W24-F003 (the livedata tier is advisory) — fixing only the artifact still leaves these 22 non-blocking.

title: 286 tests run only in a `continue-on-error` step, and at least 46 of them open zero files under exports/, CSVs/ or data/ — pure logic exempted from the blocking gate by a filename rule
claimUnderTest: tests/conftest.py:78-86: 'A handful of tests assert against the LIVE scraped board ... Mark these modules ``livedata`` so CI runs them as a NON-blocking advisory tier while the pure-logic suite stays the hard gate.' tests/test_livedata_policy.py exists to check 'the exemption list, checked instead of trusted'.
observed: The marker is applied by FILE BASENAME (`item.path.name`), not by whether the test touches live data, so it exempts whole modules including their purely synthetic halves. Measured with a `sys.addaudithook('open')` probe over each livedata module: tests/scripts/test_fetch_flock_fantasy_rookies.py (24 tests) and tests/adapters/test_dlf_scraper.py (9 tests) open ZERO paths under exports/, CSVs/ or data/. tests/api/test_dlf_source.py opens exactly one (data/snapshots/ranks_last.json), and 9 of its 13 tests live in the two classes (TestDlfCsvPreprocessor, TestDlfCsvEnrichment) that build temp CSVs — the second of which tests/test_livedata_policy.py's own docstring records as 'STILL OPEN, deliberately not fixed here'. tests/canonical/test_ktc_reconciliation.py opens one file but carries 13 tests. Total collected under `-m livedata`: 286 of 6,326. The policy test pins only two historical cases (test_pick_rookie_anchor_core.py and test_footballguys_source.py) and has no general check, so a new over-broad entry is undetectable.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && PYTHONPATH=docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W24 W24_IOPROBE_OUT=/tmp/w24-io.txt .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_fetch_flock_fantasy_rookies.py tests/adapters/test_dlf_scraper.py 'tests/api/test_dlf_source.py::TestDlfCsvEnrichment' 'tests/api/test_dlf_source.py::TestDlfCsvPreprocessor' -p ioprobe -q --tb=no 2>&1 | tail -3 && .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ --co -q -m livedata 2>&1 | tail -1
reproduction.expected: livedata-marked tests read live data; otherwise they belong in the blocking tier
reproduction.actual: '[ioprobe] 0 distinct paths under exports/ CSVs/ data/' with '40 passed in 0.23s'; and '286/6326 tests collected (6040 deselected)'

userImpact: A PR that breaks the DLF CSV preprocessor, the DLF scraper's HTML parsing, or the Flock Fantasy rookie fetcher's row mapping merges green: those 46 tests report in a step marked `continue-on-error: true`. DLF is a voting source on the live board and Flock supplies the rookie ladder, so the regression lands in production values with the PR check showing a tick.

priorFinding.note: Prior named tests/api/test_data_contract.py (33 tests) and tests/adapters/test_dlf_scraper.py (9). The data_contract half WAS fixed — conftest.py:103-118 records the removal on 2026-08-04 as 'audit finding Q-1'. test_dlf_scraper.py was never removed, and I add two more modules plus an audit-hook I/O proof rather than a source read.

whatWorks: The blocking/advisory split itself is sound and well-motivated (a yahooBoone row-count dip should not block every PR), and tests/test_livedata_policy.py does correctly prevent the two specific regressions it names. tests/api/test_pick_rookie_anchor_core.py is a real, verified rescue: 9 tests with 10 numeric-literal assertions, in the blocking tier.
rootCause: tests/conftest.py:143 keys the marker on `item.path.name`, a whole-file granularity the file itself defends as 'one central, reviewable policy instead of editing ~16 files'. Correctness is per-test, not per-file.
requiredRepair: Move the three pure-logic modules/classes out of _LIVEDATA_MODULES (the same split already done for test_pick_rookie_anchor_core.py), and generalise tests/test_livedata_policy.py to run the I/O audit-hook probe over every exempted module and fail on any that opens nothing under exports/ CSVs/ data/. The probe is 40 lines: docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W24/ioprobe.py.
dependencies: PRIOR-A08-F09 (basename collisions) is still latent and would become active the moment a colliding basename is added: 6 collisions exist today (test_calibration, test_endpoint, test_replacement, test_scoring, test_service x5, test_store), none currently matching a livedata entry.

title: e2e.yml's SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1 skips all 13 tests in both visual specs — including the structural assertions the workflow's own comment claims still run
claimUnderTest: .github/workflows/e2e.yml:207-209 states: 'Visual-regression baselines are not committed to the repo, so pixel comparisons are skipped; the visual specs still run their structural chart/render assertions.' public-league-visual.spec.js:145-149 similarly says 'each test must now stand on a data-derived structural assertion that fails when the section breaks.'
observed: Both specs call `test.skip(!!process.env.SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION, ...)` in the DESCRIBE BODY, not inside a test. In Playwright that skips every test in the group. With SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1 set at e2e.yml:210, all 9 tests in chart-visual-regression.spec.js and all 4 in public-league-visual.spec.js are skipped — including `Hill curve has axis + at least one path`, `Confidence scatter has enough points`, and the four /league section content assertions, none of which take a screenshot. The `--ignore-snapshots` flag on the same command would already have neutered the 14 `toHaveScreenshot` calls on its own (zero .png baselines are committed), so the env var buys nothing and costs the structural half. Reproduced with a two-test Playwright fixture using the identical pattern: 2 passed without the var, 2 skipped with it.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && echo '--- without ---' && node_modules/.bin/playwright test -c docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W24/pwrepro/pw.config.js 2>&1 | tail -3 && echo '--- with SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1 ---' && SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1 node_modules/.bin/playwright test -c docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W24/pwrepro/pw.config.js 2>&1 | tail -3 && echo '--- committed pixel baselines ---' && git ls-files 'tests/e2e/**/*.png' | wc -l
reproduction.expected: the structural (non-screenshot) test still runs when SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1
reproduction.actual: '2 passed (765ms)' without the var; '2 skipped' with it — the structural test is skipped too. 0 committed .png baselines.

userImpact: The Hill-curve methodology panel, the tier-gap waterfall, the confidence scatter, the matchup-margin histogram, the trade-flow Sankey, the activity heatmap and the franchise trajectory can all render blank on /rankings and /league with no CI signal at any cadence — nightly, PR, or deploy. The four /league section renderers (Records, Streaks, Awards, Recaps) are in the same position. e2e.yml is the ONLY workflow that runs these specs, and prod-e2e-smoke.yml runs only public-league.spec.js.

priorFinding.note: Prior established that the visual half is disabled in the only workflow that runs it. New here: runtime proof of the describe-body skip semantics, and the identification that e2e.yml's own inline comment asserts the opposite ('the visual specs still run their structural chart/render assertions') — which is what makes this survive review. tests/e2e/README.md:108 states it correctly ('Skip the two visual-regression specs entirely'), so the workflow comment is the outlier.

whatWorks: The rest of the E2E suite is genuinely non-vacuous: I re-verified a sample of docs/e2e-assertion-audit.md's own findings and they have been remediated — critical-smoke.spec.js:159-160 now asserts `expect(url).toContain('/login')` with the `|| body.length > 0` disjunction removed (finding A6), and signed-in-smoke.spec.js now anchors on page <h1>s and live-contract data instead of nav-label regexes (A1-A3). journey-tools-health.spec.js:60-66 asserts BOTH branches instead of skipping.
rootCause: `test.skip(condition, description)` in a describe body is a group-level modifier, but reads like a per-test guard; the workflow author assumed it only gated the screenshots.
requiredRepair: Drop `SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION: "1"` from e2e.yml — `--ignore-snapshots` already suppresses the pixel comparisons — or move the `test.skip` into the seven screenshot tests only, leaving the structural ones ungated. Then correct the workflow comment.
dependencies: None. `--ignore-snapshots` remains correct while no baselines are committed.

title: The Sleeper league-context fetch in `_resolve_league_context` — which derives the roster count that sets all 72 slot-pick values — executes in zero tests, proven with a urlopen spy
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md pipeline step 13 and data_contract.py:8356-8360: 'Pick (round, slot) inherits the rankDerivedValue of the rookie at position (round-1)*N + slot in the merged rookie list, where N is the operator's Sleeper league roster count resolved via ``_resolve_league_context``.' tests/conftest.py:33-35 concedes 'the live derivation branch is NOT exercised by this suite'.
observed: Confirmed and quantified. conftest.py:43 pops SLEEPER_LEAGUE_ID and :52 points LEAGUE_REGISTRY_PATH at /nonexistent/path/for/tests.json, so `league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id()` returns None, the env fallback is empty, and `_resolve_league_context` returns its fallback dict at line 6218 — 30 lines BEFORE the network call. I installed a urlopen spy that raises on any call and ran the function under the exact conftest environment: zero calls attempted, context = {'roster_count': 12, 'bonus_rec_te': 0.0, 'fetched_from_sleeper': False}. So the URL construction, the `total_rosters` parse, the `bonus_rec_te` float coercion, the `size > 0` guard, the 1h cache fill and the exception fallback have no coverage anywhere in 6,326 tests. `_derive_tep_multiplier_from_league` IS well covered (tests/api/test_source_overrides.py:864-887 pins 1.0/1.15/1.30/clamp/garbage), but only via injected dicts — never a dict this function produced.

reproduction.command:
cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && cat > /tmp/w24_ctx_probe.py <<'PY'
import urllib.request
from src.api import data_contract as dc
calls = []
def _spy(*a, **k):
    calls.append(str(a[0]))
    raise AssertionError('network attempted')
urllib.request.urlopen = _spy
dc._LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE.clear()
dc._LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE['context'] = None
dc._LEAGUE_CONTEXT_CACHE['fetched_at'] = 0.0
print('context:', dc._resolve_league_context())
print('urlopen calls:', calls)
print('roster_count N:', dc._resolve_league_roster_count())
PY
.venv/bin/python -c "import runpy, sys; sys.argv=['x']; import tests.conftest; runpy.run_path('/tmp/w24_ctx_probe.py', run_name='__main__')" 2>&1 | tail -3
reproduction.expected: at least one test drives the Sleeper branch
reproduction.actual: context: {'roster_count': 12, 'bonus_rec_te': 0.0, 'fetched_from_sleeper': False} / urlopen calls: [] / roster_count N: 12 — the fallback, with no network attempted

userImpact: The fallback N=12 happens to equal dynasty_main's real teamCount today, so the board is correct by coincidence. If the operator's league moves to 10 or 14 teams, or Sleeper renames `total_rosters`, every slot pick past round 1 tethers to the wrong rookie — a round-3 pick 1.01 in a 10-team league should index rookie 21, not rookie 25 — and no test in the repository fails. dynasty_new already has teamCount 10 in config/leagues/registry.json, so the divergence exists in the shipped config. The same branch supplies bonus_rec_te, which sets the TE-premium multiplier for every TE row.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the untested Sleeper-derivation branch. conftest.py's own comment (lines 31-35) admits it, which is why this is stated as a confirmed-and-quantified gap rather than a discovery — the contribution is the runtime proof and the blast radius.

whatWorks: `_derive_tep_multiplier_from_league` is properly unit-tested with injected contexts, including the clamp and the `fetched_from_sleeper=False` distrust rule (test_source_overrides.py:1026-1031). The isolation itself is correct policy — a live fetch in unit tests would make every TE fixture depend on the commissioner's settings.
rootCause: The isolation is applied at the environment level (env vars) rather than at the seam, so there is no cheap way to drive the branch; nothing forces a compensating test.
requiredRepair: Add one test that monkeypatches `urllib.request.urlopen` with a canned Sleeper league payload and asserts (a) roster_count comes from `total_rosters`, (b) bonus_rec_te coercion of a string/None/negative, (c) `size > 0` rejects a zero, (d) the cache fills and the TTL is honoured, (e) an exception yields the fallback. Then add a pick-ladder test at N=10 and N=14.
dependencies: W24-F006 (the registry is neutralized by the same conftest lines).

title: No test exercises the shipped config/leagues/registry.json through any endpoint; under conftest `leagues_share_scoring` is always False, inverting the production answer for the repo's two live leagues
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: '`/api/data`, `/api/rankings/overrides` — 503 only when scoring profiles genuinely differ. When they match but sleeper is for a different league, serve shared rankings with `sleeper: null` + `sleeperDataReady: false`.' The registry is the single source of truth for that decision.
observed: Under the default test environment the registry is empty: `active_leagues()` returns [], `get_default_league()` returns None, and `leagues_share_scoring('dynasty_main','dynasty_new')` returns **False**. In production both leagues carry scoringProfile 'superflex_tep15_ppr1', so the same call returns **True** — the two branches of the CLAUDE.md rule are inverted between the test environment and production. `GET /api/leagues` answers `{"leagues":[],"defaultKey":null}` under conftest versus two full league blocks on the live server. The profile-match branch IS covered, but only against synthetic registries written to tmp_path (test_league_routing.py:332-348 builds its own two-same-one-different set); the shipped registry.json reaches the production parser in exactly one place, tests/api/test_config_parity.py:163-172, which asserts only shape (non-zero leagues, non-'default' profile) and never routes a request through it.

reproduction.command:
cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && cat > /tmp/w24_reg.py <<'PY'
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import server
from src.api import league_registry as lr
print('active_leagues:', [c.key for c in lr.active_leagues()])
print('default:', lr.get_default_league())
print('share_scoring(main,new):', lr.leagues_share_scoring('dynasty_main','dynasty_new'))
print('GET /api/leagues ->', TestClient(server.app).get('/api/leagues').text[:80])
PY
.venv/bin/python -c "import runpy, sys; sys.argv=['x']; import tests.conftest; runpy.run_path('/tmp/w24_reg.py', run_name='__main__')" 2>&1 | grep -E 'active_leagues|default:|share_scoring|GET /api' && echo '--- live server ---' && curl -s -b /tmp/w24-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/leagues | head -c 120
reproduction.expected: the test environment resolves the same two leagues production does
reproduction.actual: active_leagues: [] / default: None / share_scoring(main,new): False / GET /api/leagues -> {"leagues":[],"defaultKey":null}  — while the live server returns dynasty_main + dynasty_new, both 'superflex_tep15_ppr1'

numericProof.formula: leagues_share_scoring(a,b) = get_league_by_key(a).scoring_profile == get_league_by_key(b).scoring_profile, False when either resolves to None

userImpact: A typo, a renamed scoringProfile, an `active: false`, or a malformed rosterSettings block in config/leagues/registry.json changes which league a request resolves to and whether /api/data 503s — and no test that routes a request would notice, because every routing test builds its own registry. The shipped file is checked only for 'parses, non-empty, profile not literally "default"'. dynasty_main (12 teams, IDP, best-ball) and dynasty_new (10 teams, no IDP, no best-ball) differ on every axis that drives roster constraints, so a registry regression silently mis-shapes the starter counts and flex rules the trade and roster surfaces enforce.

priorFinding.note: No prior A08 finding covers the registry neutralization. Distinct from W24-F005: that one is about the Sleeper HTTP fetch, this one about the registry file itself never reaching an endpoint under test.

whatWorks: tests/api/test_league_routing.py is thorough on the routing LOGIC (unknown_league, inactive_league, aliases, same-profile vs different-profile, the sleeperDataReady stamp) against synthetic registries — 3 separate fixture registries, one of which deliberately encodes the two-same-one-different profile shape. tests/api/test_config_parity.py correctly restores and then restores-back LEAGUE_REGISTRY_PATH in setUpClass/tearDownClass so it does not leak.
rootCause: conftest.py:52 points the registry at a nonexistent path to prevent live Sleeper fetches — a correct goal achieved with an instrument that also removes the shipped configuration from every test.
requiredRepair: Point LEAGUE_REGISTRY_PATH at the real config/leagues/registry.json and prevent the network at the fetch seam instead (monkeypatch `urllib.request.urlopen` in conftest to raise). That keeps league resolution real while keeping the suite offline, and would let the existing routing tests run against the shipped file.
dependencies: W24-F005 — the same two conftest lines cause both.

title: `percentile_to_value` — the live conversion behind every displayed player value — has zero absolute numeric assertions in 6,326 tests; every expectation is either relational or computed by calling the function itself
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md pipeline step 3: 'Hill-style percentile-to-value conversion via scope-level master curves in src/canonical/player_valuation.py' — the step that turns every rank-signal source's vote into a number a user reads.
observed: `percentile_to_value` is called at data_contract.py:7611/7619/7621 inside `_compute_unified_rankings`, i.e. it is the live path. Grepping every test reference and its following three lines for an absolute numeric comparison (>=3 digits, assertAlmostEqual, or approx) returns nothing. What exists instead: boundedness (test_fitted_curve_bounds.py:229, a hypothesis-style sweep), monotonicity, and — in test_percentile_reference_resolution.py:52-61, test_single_curve_live.py:525-527, test_rank_history.py:269-270 — expectations produced by calling `percentile_to_value`/`rank_to_value_for_scope` with the same constants the implementation uses. Those are routing/plumbing checks, honest as such, but the arithmetic is verified against itself. The one absolute freeze guard in the tree, tests/canonical/test_player_valuation.py:134-144 ({1:9999, 2:9781, ... 500:1360}), pins `rank_to_value` — the LEGACY rank-form curve used for rank-history reconstruction — not `percentile_to_value`, and its own comment instructs 'regenerate this dict from the constants rather than hand-editing it', which is a change detector by construction.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && echo '--- absolute numeric pins on percentile_to_value output (expect: none) ---' && grep -rn 'percentile_to_value' tests/ --include=*.py -A3 | grep -E '==\s*[0-9]{3,}|assertEqual.*[0-9]{3,}|approx\([0-9]' | wc -l && echo '--- confirm it is the live path ---' && grep -n 'percentile_to_value' src/api/data_contract.py | head -5 && echo '--- the one absolute pin, on the OTHER function ---' && sed -n '120,124p;134,136p' tests/canonical/test_player_valuation.py
reproduction.expected: at least one test pins a percentile_to_value output against an independently derived number
reproduction.actual: 0 absolute pins; the function is live at data_contract.py:7611/7619/7621; the only absolute dict pins `rank_to_value`, the legacy rank-form curve

userImpact: An arithmetic change to the Hill sigmoid — a sign flip in the exponent, a wrong clamp bound, an off-by-one in the percentile denominator — would move every rank-signal-derived value on the 1,092-row board while keeping monotonicity and boundedness intact, and no test would fail. The user reads a repriced board on /rankings and trades against it.

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the rank_to_value dict as a self-regenerated freeze guard and was explicit that it 'pins nothing about correctness'. New here: the observation that the guarded function is the LEGACY curve, and that the LIVE conversion (percentile_to_value) has no absolute pin at all — so the freeze guard is on the wrong function.

whatWorks: Numeric pinning is genuinely strong elsewhere in the pipeline. tests/api/test_market_corridor_clamp.py has 31 tests with 26 numeric-literal assertions including exact clamped outputs (4500, 5500, 5750) and stamp fields (marketAnchor 3600, bandPct 0.15). tests/api/test_count_aware_blend.py pins 15 exact centers/MADs. tests/trade/test_faab_bid_parity.py + frontend/__tests__/faab-bid-parity.test.js share tests/fixtures/faab_bid_parity_cases.json whose header states 'Every `expected` below is hand-derived from the formula in `rounding`, not produced by running either implementation' — a genuinely non-tautological cross-language oracle. tests/bdvm/test_engine_parity.py checks against a reference transcribed from a published PDF.
rootCause: The stated reason (tests/api/test_golden_dataset_invariants.py:24-27) is that 'the Hill constants are refit weekly by an automated workflow, so asserting Player X is worth 8,412 would make a legitimate refit look like a regression'. That rationale is now stale: per CLAUDE.md and ADR-008, the refit no longer ships constants — promotion is a manual `scripts/model_registry.py promote` + `apply` — so constants only move when a human moves them.
requiredRepair: Add a freeze guard for `percentile_to_value` in the same style as the rank_to_value dict, keyed to the promoted constants (10 points across the percentile range), and place it beside the existing tripwire in tests/canonical/test_hill_percentile_constants_tripwire.py so a promotion updates one place and an accidental arithmetic edit fails.

title: tests/consensus_edge/test_scoring.py:301 asserts a cached object's field against itself and cannot detect an unstable paramSetId
claimUnderTest: `test_param_set_id_is_stable` — the name asserts that the content-hashed parameter-set identifier is reproducible across calls, which is what makes a payload's `paramSetId` a meaningful version stamp.
observed: `self.assertEqual(params_mod.load()['paramSetId'], params_mod.load()['paramSetId'])`. `params.load()` memoizes into a module-level `_CACHE` (params.py:25) and returns it verbatim on any subsequent call with `path=None, refresh=False` (params.py:61-62). Both sides of the assertion are therefore the same dict object's same key — the equality is `x == x` on one object. A paramSetId derived from `id()`, a timestamp, or unstable dict ordering would pass this test unchanged, because the hash is computed exactly once.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && sed -n '300,302p' tests/consensus_edge/test_scoring.py && echo '--- the cache that makes it x == x ---' && sed -n '58,63p' src/consensus_edge/params.py && .venv/bin/python -c "import tests.conftest; from src.consensus_edge import params; a=params.load(); b=params.load(); print('same object:', a is b)"
reproduction.actual: 'same object: True' — load() returns the cached dict, so the assertion compares one value to itself

numericProof.formula: independentComputations = calls that miss the cache

userImpact: `paramSetId` is the version stamp on every consensus-edge payload, used to tell whether two boards were produced by the same parameters. If it stopped being content-derived, cached responses and stored verdicts would be compared under a stamp that no longer identifies anything, and the only test named for that property would stay green. Impact is bounded because the `consensus_edge` flag defaults off (ADR-023).

priorFinding.note: Found by an AST scan for self-comparison across all 5,867 python test functions; it is one of only three hits, and the only one that is genuinely vacuous.

whatWorks: The other two self-comparisons found by the same scan are legitimate: tests/api/test_golden_dataset_invariants.py:228 `assert v == v` is a documented NaN check, and tests/test_trade_suggestions.py:701 `rank_score(s) == rank_score(s)` genuinely fails if rank_score becomes non-deterministic. The neighbouring test `test_comments_do_not_affect_the_id` IS a real check on `_strip_comments`. The mock-echo class is effectively absent suite-wide: an AST scan for 'asserts a literal the test installed on a mock' returned 4 hits, all legitimate pass-through contracts.
rootCause: The test was written against an API that looks pure but memoizes.
requiredRepair: `self.assertEqual(params_mod.load(refresh=True)['paramSetId'], params_mod.load(refresh=True)['paramSetId'])`, or compute the id from a re-parsed copy of the config.

title: tests/fixtures/golden/baseline.json is a 722 KB committed 'golden baseline' that no test and no workflow reads

Repo-wide grep of tests/ and .github/ for 'baseline.json', 'golden_board' or 'board_diff' returns zero hits outside those two scripts. userImpact: None directly. The cost is misdirection: a reader auditing coverage sees a committed golden board under tests/fixtures/ and reasonably concludes the full board is regression-pinned. priorFinding.note: Prior named two self-regenerated golden fixtures (the rank_to_value dict and the BDVM reference output). This is a third and a different failure mode — not 'regenerated from the code under test' but 'read by nothing at all'.

whatWorks: tests/api/test_golden_dataset_invariants.py is well built and honest: a 20-player hand-authored cross-section covering suffixes, punctuation, accents, apostrophes, IDP families, a single-source player, a contested player, picks and an unrankable OL, with a docstring that states plainly it pins invariants rather than magic numbers and routes constant checks through the module constant (`_SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION`, `OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT`) so a deliberate change updates one place.
rootCause: A developer diffing tool's output was committed into the test fixtures tree without a consumer.
requiredRepair: Either wire it into a test that diffs the freshly built contract against it with a tolerance band, or move it out of tests/fixtures/ to make its manual-tool status legible.

title: 104 python tests and 40 frontend assertions verify behavior by grepping source text, so they pass on a comment, a dead branch, or an unreachable code path
claimUnderTest: Test names such as `test_reads_backend_canonical_consensus_rank`, `test_the_consumer_reads_the_key_the_producer_writes`, `test_build_rows_is_pure_materializer` assert behavioral properties.
observed: An AST scan across 5,867 python test functions finds 104 whose ONLY assertions are substring membership against text read via `read_text()`/`getsource()`. The frontend has 40 such `expect(src).toContain(...)` assertions out of 3,708 total. The POSITIVE ones are the weak half: `assert 'canonicalConsensusRank' in src` (test_rankings_our_rank.py:99) passes if the identifier appears in a comment or in a branch that never executes; `expect(page).toContain('platform: source')` passes on a string in dead JSX.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W24/greptests_scan.py | head -3 && echo '--- frontend ---' && cd frontend && grep -rnE 'expect\((src|source|page|pageSource|clientSource|route|text|css)[A-Za-z]*\)\.(toContain|toMatch|not)' __tests__ | wc -l

userImpact: Low individually, and this class is small (1.8% python, 1.1% frontend). The risk is concentrated in the cross-file wiring tests (`test_the_consumer_reads_the_key_the_producer_writes`, `test_both_callers_go_through_the_shared_resolver`), where a grep test reads as proof that two modules agree while proving only that a string is present in both.

priorFinding.note: Prior measured the frontend as 92.6% non-numeric across 97 files. I measure the current 104-file suite and separate the specific 'grep test' subclass from legitimate render/shape assertions, which the prior's numeric-literal counter conflated.

whatWorks: The NEGATIVE grep tests are well constructed and genuinely useful: tests/api/test_rankings_our_rank.py strips comments before asserting absence (so an explanatory mention of a removed identifier is not a false failure), and tests/api/test_frontend_migration.py:37-40 matches on `def {symbol}(` rather than a bare mention for exactly that reason. Frontend fixtures are NOT tautological: frontend/__tests__/fixtures/players.js is hand-authored, and the four parity fixtures (faab_bid_parity_cases.json, signal_parity_cases.json, name_key_cases.json, trade_grade_parity_cases.json) are shared cross-language oracles that neither side may hardcode against.
rootCause: Wiring between a python producer and a JS consumer has no runtime seam in either test suite, so a source grep is the cheapest available check.
requiredRepair: For the wiring cases, replace the grep with a round-trip: build the producer's payload in python, write it to a fixture, and have the vitest half read the key off that fixture — the pattern faab-bid-parity already uses successfully.
